newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends soft on primary auction forecast.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends soft on primary auction forecast.

text.p: The Mexican peso closed softer against the dollar for the second day in a row on Tuesday after zigzagging through the session on changing predictions surrounding the central bank auction due later in the day.
"The peso was under pressure from short-covering in dollars this morning. Most players were local and trading moved in line with the outlook for (primary) interest rates," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate closed 0.5 and 0.4 of a centavo weaker, respectively, at 7.980/7.8010 and 7.7940/7.7980 per dollar.
Same-day peso contracts closed earlier 3.3 centavos weaker at 7.7950/7.8000 per dollar.
A Reuters survey of nine money market traders showed they expected bellwether 28-day Cetes rates to fall at Banco de Mexico's primary auction by an average of 52 basis points to 19.17 percent.
Banco de Mexico is due to announce the results of this week's auction at 1830 local time.
Traders said original estimated falls of up to 100 basis points were revised downwards by the notable lack of foreign traders buying pesos to participate in the auction.
"It is now felt Cetes rates may move sideways to take a breather after sharp reductions in recent weeks," a trader said.

Dealers said peso trading levels on Wednesday would be largely determined by the outcome of the Cetes auction and how the U.S. bond market would react to consumer price data to be announced in early trade.
